channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Evere proposes to name square after shopkeeper who died defending a woman on a tram
item.description: Driss Atounane, 54, was attacked in late July after he defended a woman who was being verbally abused.

item.title: Brussels Security Council to meet on Wednesday after spate of shootings
item.description: “Drug dealers are a plague and we must do everything we can to tackle the drugs trade at its root."

item.title: Brussels secures new line of credit from the Spanish bank BBVA
item.description: The move forms part of the region’s financial strategy to bolster liquidity reserves and diversify its sources of funding.

item.title: City of Brussels Mayor accused of conflict of interest over casino concession
item.description: The accusation is related to the decision in July to grant the casino concession to Napoleon Games rather than the current operator, Viage.

item.title: Saint-Gilles shootings: Rally against organised crime to take place on Sunday
item.description: According to the organisers, the gathering is also intended to put “conviviality and cohesion” back at the centre of life on the municipality’s streets.

item.title: Brussels' former MIMA museum to reopen as new music hub
item.description: From October, a new music centre will open inside the former modern art museum with rehearsal studios, concert venues and a rooftop bar.

item.title: The Brussels International Film Festival unveils details of its 9th edition
item.description: Organisers of the Brussels International Film Festival give a glimpse of the lineup for its 9th edition, to be held in the Belgian capital from 4 to 12 September.

item.title: Two possible suspects arrested in shootings Brussels
item.description: Police in Saint-Gilles arrested two people overnight who may be linked to one or more of the recent shootings in Brussels, and seized two military-grade weapons, two handguns and other items.

item.title: Brussels plans to completely redesign the Place du Nouveau Marché aux Grains in 2027
item.description: Brussels has applied for planning permission to redesign the New Grain Market, with the aim of creating more space for trees, planting, play, sport and socialising by 2027.

item.title: What are Belgium's latest food and drink tips?
item.description: Here are some of Brussels' most newest drinks, coolest cafés and intriguing restaurants.

item.title: Brussels records 57 shootings in seven months: New record year looms
item.description: A large proportion of the shootings appear to be linked to drug trafficking.

item.title: Yellow drought alert maintained in Brussels
item.description: Brussels authorities keep the yellow drought alert in place across Brussels/Capital Region despite cooler temperatures and recent rainfall.

item.title: Brussels shootings: Socialist party PS calls for meeting with Justice and Interior ministers
item.description: The party said the shootings in recent days, including one targeting a police station, were unacceptable and required a strong response from the authorities.

item.title: One person shot in the leg in Molenbeek
item.description: Police have opened an investigation into the circumstances of that shooting, but no suspects have been arrested so far.

item.title: Final tribute to Brussels firefighter Olivier Francotte at Koekelberg Basilica
item.description: Over 100 firefighters and police officers formed a guard of honour for the state funeral of Olivier Francotte, who died while on duty in August.

item.title: One person injured in latest shooting in Saint-Gilles
item.description: Police were called at around 02:40 on Monday to a possible shooting on Chaussée de Forest.

item.title: Hook-up culture and hidden homophobia: Dating in Brussels as a gay man
item.description: From Grindr to chemsex, two gay men spoke to The Brussels Times about the challenges they have faced when dating in the Belgian capital.

item.title: Anti-Slave Remembrance Day: EU exhibition asks what remains of European colonialism
item.description: On the International Day for Remembrance of the Slave trade and its Abolition, a difficult question is raised: have the former European colonial powers truly come to terms with their past?

item.title: Mayor of Saint-Gilles demands 80 extra policemen following latest shootings
item.description: According to Spinette, merging Brussels’ police zones would not in itself be a sufficient solution.

item.title: Two cars found on fire in Saint-Gilles on Saturday night
item.description: Commune's mayor said he suspected an intimidation tactic between rival gangs, while stressing that it was hypothesis.
